subsection.heading: Short Title.—
subsection.content: This Act may be cited as the “Federal Agriculture Improvement and Reform Act of 1996”.

subsection.heading: Short Title.—
subsection.content: This title may be cited as the “Agricultural Market Transition Act”.

subsection.heading: Purpose.—
subsection.chapeau: It is the purpose of this title—

paragraph.content: to authorize the use of binding production flexibility contracts between the United States and agricultural producers to support farming certainty and flexibility while ensuring continued compliance with farm conservation and wetland protection requirements;
to make nonrecourse marketing assistance loans and loan deficiency payments available for certain crops;
to improve the operation of farm programs for milk, peanuts, and sugar; and
to establish a commission to undertake a comprehensive review of past and future production agriculture in the United States.

subsection.chapeau: In this title:

paragraph.heading: Agricultural act of 1949.—
paragraph.content: Except in section 171, the term “Agricultural Act of 1949” means the Agricultural Act of 1949 (7 U.S.C. 1421 et seq.), as in effect prior to the suspensions under section 171(b)(1).

paragraph.heading: Considered planted.—
paragraph.content: The term “considered planted” means acreage that is considered planted under title V of the Agricultural Act of 1949 (7 U.S.C. 1461 et seq.) and such other acreage as the Secretary considers fair and equitable.

paragraph.heading: Contract.—
paragraph.content: The terms “contract” and “production flexibility contract” mean a production flexibility contract entered into under section 111.

paragraph.heading: Contract acreage.—
paragraph.content: The term “contract acreage” means 1 or more crop acreage bases established for contract commodities under title V of the Agricultural Act of 1949 (7 U.S.C. 1461 et seq.) that would have been in effect for the 1996 crop (but for suspension under section 171(b)(1)).

paragraph.heading: Contract commodity.—
paragraph.content: The term “contract commodity” means wheat, corn, grain sorghum, barley, oats, upland cotton, and rice.

paragraph.heading: Contract payment.—
paragraph.content: The term “contract payment” means a payment made under this subtitle pursuant to a contract.

paragraph.heading: Department.—
paragraph.content: The term “Department” means the Department of Agriculture.

paragraph.heading: Extra long staple cotton.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term “extra long staple cotton” means cotton that—

subparagraph.content: is produced from pure strain varieties of the Barbadense species or any hybrid thereof, or other similar types of extra long staple cotton, designated by the Secretary, having characteristics needed for various end uses for which United States upland cotton is not suitable and grown in irrigated cotton-growing regions of the United States designated by the Secretary or other areas designated by the Secretary as suitable for the production of the varieties or types; and
is ginned on a roller-type gin or, if authorized by the Secretary, ginned on another type gin for experimental purposes.

paragraph.heading: Farm program payment yield.—
paragraph.content: The term “farm program payment yield” means the farm program payment yield established for the 1995 crop of a contract commodity under section 505 of the Agricultural Act of 1949 (7 U.S.C. 1465). The Secretary shall adjust the farm program payment yield for the 1995 crop of a contract commodity to account for any additional yield payments made with respect to that crop under subsection (b)(2) of the section.

paragraph.heading: Loan commodity.—
paragraph.content: The term “loan commodity” means each contract commodity, extra long staple cotton, and oilseed.

paragraph.heading: Oilseed.—
paragraph.content: The term “oilseed” means a crop of soybeans, sunflower seed, rapeseed, canola, safflower, flaxseed, mustard seed, or, if designated by the Secretary, other oilseeds.

paragraph.heading: Producer.—
paragraph.content: The term “producer” means an owner, operator, landlord, tenant, or sharecropper who shares in the risk of producing a crop and who is entitled to share in the crop available for marketing from the farm, or would have shared had the crop been produced. In determining whether a grower of hybrid seed is a producer, the Secretary shall not take into consideration the existence of a hybrid seed contract.

paragraph.heading: Secretary.—
paragraph.content: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of Agriculture.

paragraph.heading: State.—
paragraph.content: The term “State” means each of the several States of the United States, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, and any other territory or possession of the United States.

paragraph.heading: United states.—
paragraph.content: The term “United States”, when used in a geographical sense, means all of the States.

section.heading: AUTHORIZATION FOR USE OF PRODUCTION FLEXIBILITY CONTRACTS.

subsection.heading: Offer and Terms.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall offer to enter into a production flexibility contract with an eligible owner or producer described in subsection (b) on a farm containing eligible cropland. Under the terms of a contract, the owner or producer shall agree, in exchange for annual contract payments, to—

paragraph.content: comply with applicable conservation requirements under subtitle B of title XII of the Food Security Act of 1985 (16 U.S.C. 3811 et seq.);
comply with applicable wetland protection requirements under subtitle C of title XII of the Act (16 U.S.C. 3821 et seq.);
comply with the planting flexibility requirements of section 118; and
use the land subject to the contract for an agricultural or related activity, but not for a nonagricultural commercial or industrial use, as determined by the Secretary.

subsection.heading: Eligible Owners and Producers Described.—
subsection.chapeau: The following producers and owners shall be eligible to enter into a contract:

paragraph.content: An owner of eligible cropland who assumes all or a part of the risk of producing a crop.
A producer (other than an owner) on eligible cropland with a share-rent lease of the eligible cropland, regardless of the length of the lease, if the owner enters into the same contract.

A producer (other than an owner) on eligible cropland who cash rents the eligible cropland under a lease expiring on or after September 30, 2002, in which case the owner is not required to enter into the contract.

A producer (other than an owner) on eligible cropland who cash rents the eligible cropland under a lease expiring before September 30, 2002. The owner of the eligible cropland may also enter into the same contract. If the producer elects to enroll less than 100 percent of the eligible cropland in the contract, the consent of the owner is required.

An owner of eligible cropland who cash rents the eligible cropland and the lease term expires before September 30, 2002, if the tenant declines to enter into a contract. In the case of an owner covered by this paragraph, contract payments shall not begin under a contract until the lease held by the tenant ends.

An owner or producer described in any preceding paragraph regardless of whether the owner or producer purchased catastrophic risk protection for a 1996 crop under section 508(b) of the Federal Crop Insurance Act (7 U.S.C. 1508(b)).

subsection.heading: Tenants and Sharecroppers.—
subsection.content: In carrying out this subtitle, the Secretary shall provide adequate safeguards to protect the interests of tenants and sharecroppers.

subsection.heading: Eligible Cropland Described.—
subsection.chapeau: Land shall be considered to be cropland eligible for coverage under a contract only if the land has contract acreage attributable to the land and—

paragraph.content: for at least 1 of the 1991 through 1995 crops, at least a portion of the land was enrolled in the acreage reduction program authorized for a crop of a contract commodity under section 101B, 103B, 105B, or 107B of the Agricultural Act of 1949 or was considered planted;
was subject to a conservation reserve contract under section 1231 of the Food Security Act of 1985 (16 U.S.C. 3831) whose term expired, or was voluntarily terminated, on or after January 1, 1995; or
is released from coverage under a conservation reserve contract by the Secretary during the period beginning on January 1, 1995, and ending on the date specified in section 112(a)(2).

subsection.heading: Quantity of Eligible Cropland Covered by Contract.—
subsection.content: Subject to subsection (b)(4), an owner or producer may enroll as contract acreage all or a portion of the eligible cropland on the farm.

subsection.heading: Voluntary Reduction in Contract Acreage.—
subsection.content: Subject to subsection (b)(4), an owner or producer who enters into a contract may subsequently reduce the quantity of contract acreage covered by the contract.

paragraph.heading: Commencement.—
paragraph.content: To the extent practicable, the Secretary shall commence entering into contracts not later than 45 days after the date of enactment of this title.

paragraph.heading: Deadline.—
paragraph.content: Except as provided in paragraph (3), the Secretary may not enter into a contract after August 1, 1996.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: At the beginning of each fiscal year, the Secretary shall allow an eligible owner or producer on a farm covered by a conservation reserve contract entered into under section 1231 of the Food Security Act of 1985 (16 U.S.C. 3831) that terminates after the date specified in paragraph (2) to enter into or expand a production flexibility contract to cover the contract acreage of the farm that was subject to the former conservation reserve contract.

subparagraph.heading: Amount.—
subparagraph.content: Contract payments made for contract acreage under this paragraph shall be made at the rate and amount applicable to the annual contract payment level for the applicable crop. For the fiscal year in which the conservation reserve contract is terminated, the owner or producer subject to the production flexibility contract may elect to receive either contract payments or a prorated payment under the conservation reserve contract, but not both.

paragraph.heading: Beginning date.—
paragraph.chapeau: The term of a contract shall begin with—

subparagraph.content: the 1996 crop of a contract commodity; or

in the case of acreage that was subject to a conservation reserve contract described in subsection (a)(3), the date the production flexibility contract was entered into or expanded to cover the acreage.

paragraph.heading: Ending date.—
paragraph.content: The term of a contract shall extend through the 2002 crop, unless earlier terminated by the owner or producer.

subsection.heading: Estimation of Contract Payments.—
subsection.content: At the time the Secretary enters into a contract, the Secretary shall provide an estimate of the minimum contract payments anticipated to be made during at least the first fiscal year for which contract payments will be made.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: An annual contract payment shall be made not later than September 30 of each of fiscal years 1996 through 2002.

subparagraph.heading: Fiscal year 1996.—
subparagraph.content: At the option of the owner or producer, 50 percent of the contract payment for fiscal year 1996 shall be made not later than 30 days after the date on which the contract is entered into and approved by the Secretary and the owner or producer.

subparagraph.heading: Subsequent fiscal years.—
subparagraph.content: At the option of the owner or producer for fiscal year 1997 and each subsequent fiscal year, 50 percent of the annual contract payment shall be made on December 15 or January 15 of the fiscal year. The owner or producer may change the date selected under this subparagraph for a subsequent fiscal year by providing advance notice to the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Special rule.—
paragraph.content: Notwithstanding the requirements for making an annual contract payment specified in paragraphs (1) and (2), at the option of the owner or producer, the Secretary shall pay the full amount (or such portion as the owner or producer may specify) of the contract payment required to be paid for any of fiscal years 1999 through 2002 at such time or times during that fiscal year as the owner or producer may specify.

subsection.heading: Fiscal Year Amounts.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall, to the maximum extent practicable, expend the following amounts to satisfy the obligations of the Secretary under all contracts:

subsection.heading: Allocation.—
subsection.chapeau: The amount made available for a fiscal year under subsection (a) shall be allocated as follows:

paragraph.content: For wheat, 26.26 percent.
For corn, 46.22 percent.
For grain sorghum, 5.11 percent.
For barley, 2.16 percent.
For oats, 0.15 percent.
For upland cotton, 11.63 percent.
For rice, 8.47 percent.

subsection.heading: Adjustment.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall adjust the amounts allocated for each contract commodity under subsection (b) for a particular fiscal year by—

paragraph.content: adding an amount equal to the sum of all repayments of deficiency payments required under section 114(a)(2) of the Agricultural Act of 1949 (7 U.S.C. 1445j(a)(2)) for the commodity;
adding an amount equal to the sum of all refunds of contract payments received during the preceding fiscal year under section 116 for the commodity; and

subtracting an amount equal to the amount, if any, necessary during that fiscal year to satisfy payment requirements for the commodity under sections 103B, 105B, or 107B of the Agricultural Act of 1949 for the 1994 and 1995 crop years.

subsection.heading: Additional Rice Allocation.—
subsection.content: In addition to the adjustments required under subsection (c), the amount allocated under subsection (b) for rice contract payments shall be increased by $8,500,000 for each of fiscal years 1997 through 2002.

subsection.heading: Exclusion of Certain Amounts From Contract Payments.—
subsection.content: Any amount added pursuant to paragraphs (1) and (2) of subsection (c) to the amount available under subsection (a) for a fiscal year and paid to owners and producers under a contract shall not be treated as a contract payment for purposes of section 115(a) of this title or section 1001(1) of the Food Security Act of 1985 (7 U.S.C. 1308(1)). However, the amount of a payment covered by this subsection may not exceed $50,000 per person.

subsection.heading: Effect of Payment Limitation.—
subsection.content: The amount available under subsection (a) for a fiscal year shall be reduced by an amount equal to the total amount of contract payments for the fiscal year that owners and producers forgo as a result of operation of the payment limitation under section 1001(1) of the Food Security Act of 1985 (7 U.S.C. 1308(1)).

section.heading: DETERMINATION OF CONTRACT PAYMENTS UNDER CONTRACTS.

subsection.heading: Individual Payment Quantity of Contract Commodities.—
subsection.chapeau: For each contract, the payment quantity of a contract commodity for each fiscal year shall be equal to the product of—

paragraph.content: 85 percent of the contract acreage; and
the farm program payment yield.

subsection.heading: Annual Payment Quantity of Contract Commodities.—
subsection.content: The payment quantity of each contract commodity covered by all contracts for each fiscal year shall be equal to the sum of the amounts calculated under subsection (a) for each individual contract.

subsection.heading: Annual Payment Rate.—
subsection.chapeau: The payment rate for a contract commodity for each fiscal year shall be equal to—

paragraph.content: the amount made available under section 113 for the contract commodity for the fiscal year; divided by
the amount determined under subsection (b) for the fiscal year.

subsection.heading: Annual Payment Amount.—
subsection.chapeau: The amount to be paid under a contract in effect for each fiscal year with respect to all contract commodities covered by the contract shall be equal to the sum of the products of—

paragraph.content: the payment quantity determined under subsection (a) for each of the contract commodities covered by the contract; and
the corresponding payment rate for the contract commodity in effect under subsection (c).

subsection.heading: Reduction in Payment Amount.—
subsection.content: The contract payment determined under subsection (d) for an owner or producer for a fiscal year shall be immediately reduced by the amount of any repayment of deficiency payments that is required under section 114(a)(2) of the Agricultural Act of 1949 (7 U.S.C. 1445j(a)(2)) and is not repaid as of the date the contract payment is determined. The Secretary shall be required to collect the required repayment, or any claim based on the required repayment, as soon as the contract payment is determined.

subsection.heading: Assignment of Contract Payments.—
subsection.content: The provisions of section 8(g) of the Soil Conservation and Domestic Allotment Act (16 U.S.C. 590h(g)) (relating to assignment of payments) shall apply to contract payments under this section. The owner or producer making the assignment, or the assignee, shall provide the Secretary with notice, in such manner as the Secretary may require in the contract, of any assignment made under this subsection.

subsection.heading: Sharing of Contract Payments.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall provide for the sharing of contract payments among the owners and producers subject to the contract on a fair and equitable basis.

subsection.heading: Applicability of Payment Limitations.—
subsection.content: Sections 1001 through 1001C of the Food Security Act of 1985 (7 U.S.C. 1308 through 1308–3), as amended by this section, shall be applicable to contract payments made under this subtitle.

footnote.p: Sec. 115(b) amended sec. 1001 of the Food Security Act of 1985 (7 U.S.C. 1308).
Sec. 115(b) amended secs. 1001A and 1001C of the Food Security Act of 1985 (7 U.S.C. 1308–1 and 1308–3).

subsection.heading: Termination of Contract For Violation.—
subsection.content: Except as provided in subsection (b), if an owner or producer subject to a contract violates a requirement of the contract specified in section 111(a), the Secretary shall terminate the contract with respect to the owner or producer on each farm in which the owner or producer has an interest. On the termination, the owner or producer shall forfeit all rights to receive future contract payments on each farm in which the owner or producer has an interest and shall refund to the Secretary all contract payments received by the owner or producer during the period of the violation, together with interest on the contract payments as determined by the Secretary.

subsection.heading: Refund or Adjustment.—
subsection.chapeau: If the Secretary determines that a violation does not warrant termination of the contract under subsection (a), the Secretary may require the owner or producer subject to the contract—

paragraph.content: to refund to the Secretary that part of the contract payments received by the owner or producer during the period of the violation, together with interest on the contract payments as determined by the Secretary; or
to accept a reduction in the amount of future contract payments that is proportionate to the severity of the violation, as determined by the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Effect of foreclosure.—
paragraph.content: An owner or producer subject to a contract may not be required to make repayments to the Secretary of amounts received under the contract if the contract acreage has been foreclosed on and the Secretary determines that forgiving the repayments is appropriate to provide fair and equitable treatment.

paragraph.heading: Resumption of operation.—
paragraph.content: This subsection shall not void the responsibilities of the owner or producer under the contract if the owner or producer continues or resumes operation, or control, of the contract acreage. On the resumption of operation or control over the contract acreage by the owner or producer, the provisions of the contract in effect on the date of the foreclosure shall apply.

subsection.heading: Review.—
subsection.content: A determination of the Secretary under this section shall be considered to be an adverse decision for purposes of the availability of administrative review of the determination.

section.heading: TRANSFER OR CHANGE OF INTEREST IN LANDS SUBJECT TO CONTRACT.

subsection.heading: Termination.—
subsection.content: Except as provided in subsection (c), a transfer of (or change in) the interest of an owner or producer subject to a contract in the contract acreage covered by the contract shall result in the termination of the contract with respect to the acreage, unless the transferee or owner of the acreage agrees to assume all obligations under the contract. The termination shall be effective on the date of the transfer or change.

subsection.heading: Modification.—
subsection.content: At the request of the transferee or owner, the Secretary may modify the contract if the modifications are consistent with the objectives of this subtitle, as determined by the Secretary.

subsection.heading: Exception.—
subsection.content: If an owner or producer who is entitled to a contract payment dies, becomes incompetent, or is otherwise unable to receive the contract payment, the Secretary shall make the payment, in accordance with regulations prescribed by the Secretary.

subsection.heading: Permitted Crops.—
subsection.content: Subject to subsection (b), any commodity or crop may be planted on contract acreage on a farm.

subsection.heading: Limitations and Exceptions Regarding Fruits and Vegetables.—

paragraph.heading: Limitations.—
paragraph.content: The planting of fruits and vegetables (other than lentils, mung beans, and dry peas) shall be prohibited on contract acreage.

paragraph.heading: Exceptions.—
paragraph.chapeau: Paragraph (1) shall not limit the planting of a fruit or vegetable—

subparagraph.content: in any region in which there is a history of double-cropping of contract commodities with fruits or vegetables, as determined by the Secretary, in which case the double-cropping shall be permitted;

on a farm that the Secretary determines has a history of planting fruits or vegetables on contract acreage, except that a contract payment shall be reduced by an acre for each acre planted to the fruit or vegetable; or

subparagraph.chapeau: by a producer who the Secretary determines has an established planting history of a specific fruit or vegetable, except that—

clause.content: the quantity planted may not exceed the producer's average annual planting history of the fruit or vegetable in the 1991 through 1995 crop years (excluding any crop year in which no plantings were made), as determined by the Secretary; and
a contract payment shall be reduced by an acre for each acre planted to the fruit or vegetable.

subtitle.heading: Nonrecourse Marketing Assistance Loans and Loan Deficiency Payments

section.heading: AVAILABILITY OF NONRECOURSE MARKETING ASSISTANCE LOANS.

subsection.heading: Nonrecourse Loans Available.—
subsection.content: For each of the 1996 through 2002 crops of each loan commodity, the Secretary shall make available to producers on a farm nonrecourse marketing assistance loans for loan commodities produced on the farm. The loans shall be made under terms and conditions that are prescribed by the Secretary and at the loan rate established under section 132 for the loan commodity.

subsection.heading: Eligible Production.—
subsection.chapeau: The following production shall be eligible for a marketing assistance loan under subsection (a):

paragraph.content: In the case of a marketing assistance loan for a contract commodity, any production by a producer on a farm containing eligible cropland covered by a production flexibility contract.
In the case of a marketing assistance loan for extra long staple cotton and oilseeds, any production.

subsection.heading: Compliance With Conservation and Wetlands Requirements.—
subsection.content: As a condition of the receipt of a marketing assistance loan under subsection (a), the producer shall comply with applicable conservation requirements under subtitle B of title XII of the Food Security Act of 1985 (16 U.S.C. 3811 et seq.) and applicable wetland protection requirements under subtitle C of title XII of the Act (16 U.S.C. 3821 et seq.) during the term of the loan.

subsection.heading: Additional Outlays Prohibited.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall carry out this subtitle in such a manner that there are no additional outlays under this subtitle as a result of the reconstitution of a farm that occurs as a result of the combination of another farm that does not contain eligible cropland covered by a production flexibility contract.

section.heading: LOAN RATES FOR MARKETING ASSISTANCE LOANS.

paragraph.heading: Loan rate.—
paragraph.chapeau: Subject to paragraph (2), the loan rate for a marketing assistance loan under section 131 for wheat shall be—

subparagraph.content: not less than 85 percent of the simple average price received by producers of wheat, as determined by the Secretary, during the marketing years for the immediately preceding 5 crops of wheat, excluding the year in which the average price was the highest and the year in which the average price was the lowest in the period; but
not more than $2.58 per bushel.

paragraph.heading: Stocks to use ratio adjustment.—
paragraph.chapeau: If the Secretary estimates for any marketing year that the ratio of ending stocks of wheat to total use for the marketing year will be—

subparagraph.content: equal to or greater than 30 percent, the Secretary may reduce the loan rate for wheat for the corresponding crop by an amount not to exceed 10 percent in any year;
less than 30 percent but not less than 15 percent, the Secretary may reduce the loan rate for wheat for the corresponding crop by an amount not to exceed 5 percent in any year; or
less than 15 percent, the Secretary may not reduce the loan rate for wheat for the corresponding crop.

paragraph.heading: Loan rate for corn.—
paragraph.chapeau: Subject to paragraph (2), the loan rate for a marketing assistance loan under section 131 for corn shall be—

subparagraph.content: not less than 85 percent of the simple average price received by producers of corn, as determined by the Secretary, during the marketing years for the immediately preceding 5 crops of corn, excluding the year in which the average price was the highest and the year in which the average price was the lowest in the period; but
not more than $1.89 per bushel.

paragraph.heading: Stocks to use ratio adjustment.—
paragraph.chapeau: If the Secretary estimates for any marketing year that the ratio of ending stocks of corn to total use for the marketing year will be—

subparagraph.content: equal to or greater than 25 percent, the Secretary may reduce the loan rate for corn for the corresponding crop by an amount not to exceed 10 percent in any year;
less than 25 percent but not less than 12.5 percent, the Secretary may reduce the loan rate for corn for the corresponding crop by an amount not to exceed 5 percent in any year; or
less than 12.5 percent, the Secretary may not reduce the loan rate for corn for the corresponding crop.

paragraph.heading: Other feed grains.—
paragraph.content: The loan rate for a marketing assistance loan under section 131 for grain sorghum, barley, and oats, respectively, shall be established at such level as the Secretary determines is fair and reasonable in relation to the rate that loans are made available for corn, taking into consideration the feeding value of the commodity in relation to corn.

paragraph.heading: Loan rate.—
paragraph.chapeau: Subject to paragraph (2), the loan rate for a marketing assistance loan under section 131 for upland cotton shall be established by the Secretary at such loan rate, per pound, as will reflect for the base quality of upland cotton, as determined by the Secretary, at average locations in the United States a rate that is not less than the smaller of—

subparagraph.content: 85 percent of the average price (weighted by market and month) of the base quality of cotton as quoted in the designated United States spot markets during 3 years of the 5-year period ending July 31 of the year preceding the year in which the crop is planted, excluding the year in which the average price was the highest and the year in which the average price was the lowest in the period; or

90 percent of the average, for the 15-week period beginning July 1 of the year preceding the year in which the crop is planted, of the 5 lowest-priced growths of the growths quoted for Middling 13⁄32-inch cotton C.I.F. Northern Europe (adjusted downward by the average difference during the period April 15 through October 15 of the year preceding the year in which the crop is planted between the average Northern European price quotation of such quality of cotton and the market quotations in the designated United States spot markets for the base quality of upland cotton), as determined by the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Limitations.—
paragraph.content: The loan rate for a marketing assistance loan for upland cotton shall not be less than $0.50 per pound or more than $0.5192 per pound.

subsection.heading: Extra Long Staple Cotton.—
subsection.chapeau: The loan rate for a marketing assistance loan under section 131 for extra long staple cotton shall be—

paragraph.content: not less than 85 percent of the simple average price received by producers of extra long staple cotton, as determined by the Secretary, during 3 years of the 5-year period ending July 31 of the year preceding the year in which the crop is planted, excluding the year in which the average price was the highest and the year in which the average price was the lowest in the period; but
not more than $0.7965 per pound.

subsection.heading: Rice.—
subsection.content: The loan rate for a marketing assistance loan under section 131 for rice shall be $6.50 per hundredweight.

paragraph.heading: Soybeans.—
paragraph.chapeau: The loan rate for a marketing assistance loan under section 131 for soybeans shall be—

subparagraph.content: not less than 85 percent of the simple average price received by producers of soybeans, as determined by the Secretary, during the marketing years for the immediately preceding 5 crops of soybeans, excluding the year in which the average price was the highest and the year in which the average price was the lowest in the period; but
not less than $4.92 or more than $5.26 per bushel.

paragraph.heading: Sunflower seed, canola, rapeseed, safflower, mustard seed, and flaxseed.—
paragraph.chapeau: The loan rate for a marketing assistance loan under section 131 for sunflower seed, canola, rapeseed, safflower, mustard seed, and flaxseed, individually, shall be—

subparagraph.content: not less than 85 percent of the simple average price received by producers of sunflower seed, individually, as determined by the Secretary, during the marketing years for the immediately preceding 5 crops of sunflower seed, individually, excluding the year in which the average price was the highest and the year in which the average price was the lowest in the period; but
not less than $0.087 or more than $0.093 per pound.

paragraph.heading: Other oilseeds.—
paragraph.content: The loan rates for a marketing assistance loan under section 131 for other oilseeds shall be established at such level as the Secretary determines is fair and reasonable in relation to the loan rate available for soybeans, except in no event shall the rate for the oilseeds (other than cottonseed) be less than the rate established for soybeans on a per-pound basis for the same crop.

subsection.heading: Term of Loan.—
subsection.content: In the case of each loan commodity (other than upland cotton or extra long staple cotton), a marketing assistance loan under section 131 shall have a term of 9 months beginning on the first day of the first month after the month in which the loan is made.

subsection.heading: Special Rule for Cotton.—
subsection.content: A marketing assistance loan for upland cotton or extra long staple cotton shall have a term of 10 months beginning on the first day of the month in which the loan is made.

subsection.heading: Extensions Prohibited.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may not extend the term of a marketing assistance loan for any loan commodity.

subsection.heading: Repayment Rates for Wheat, Feed Grains, and Oilseeds.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall permit a producer to repay a marketing assistance loan under section 131 for wheat, corn, grain sorghum, barley, oats, and oilseeds at a rate that is the lesser of—

paragraph.content: the loan rate established for the commodity under section 132, plus interest (as determined by the Secretary); or

paragraph.chapeau: a rate that the Secretary determines will—

subparagraph.content: minimize potential loan forfeitures;
minimize the accumulation of stocks of the commodity by the Federal Government;
minimize the cost incurred by the Federal Government in storing the commodity; and
allow the commodity produced in the United States to be marketed freely and competitively, both domestically and internationally.

subsection.heading: Repayment Rates for Upland Cotton and Rice.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary shall permit producers to repay a marketing assistance loan under section 131 for upland cotton and rice at a rate that is the lesser of—

paragraph.content: the loan rate established for the commodity under section 132, plus interest (as determined by the Secretary); or
the prevailing world market price for the commodity (adjusted to United States quality and location), as determined by the Secretary.

subsection.heading: Repayment Rates for Extra Long Staple Cotton.—
subsection.content: Repayment of a marketing assistance loan for extra long staple cotton shall be at the loan rate established for the commodity under section 132, plus interest (as determined by the Secretary).

subsection.heading: Prevailing World Market Price.—
subsection.chapeau: For purposes of this section and section 136, the Secretary shall prescribe by regulation—

paragraph.content: a formula to determine the prevailing world market price for each loan commodity, adjusted to United States quality and location; and
a mechanism by which the Secretary shall announce periodically the prevailing world market price for each loan commodity.

subsection.heading: Adjustment of Prevailing World Market Price for Upland Cotton.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: During the period ending July 31, 2003, the prevailing world market price for upland cotton (adjusted to United States quality and location) established under subsection (d) shall be further adjusted if—

subparagraph.content: the adjusted prevailing world market price is less than 115 percent of the loan rate for upland cotton established under section 132, as determined by the Secretary; and

the Friday through Thursday average price quotation for the lowest-priced United States growth as quoted for Middling (M) 13⁄32-inch cotton delivered C.I.F. Northern Europe is greater than the Friday through Thursday average price of the 5 lowest-priced growths of upland cotton, as quoted for Middling (M) 13⁄32-inch cotton, delivered C.I.F. Northern Europe (referred to in this section as the “Northern Europe price”).

paragraph.heading: Further adjustment.—
paragraph.chapeau: Except as provided in paragraph (3), the adjusted prevailing world market price for upland cotton shall be further adjusted on the basis of some or all of the following data, as available:

subparagraph.content: The United States share of world exports.
The current level of cotton export sales and cotton export shipments.
Other data determined by the Secretary to be relevant in establishing an accurate prevailing world market price for upland cotton (adjusted to United States quality and location).

paragraph.heading: Limitation on further adjustment.—
paragraph.chapeau: The adjustment under paragraph (2) may not exceed the difference between—

subparagraph.content: the Friday through Thursday average price for the lowest-priced United States growth as quoted for Middling 13⁄32-inch cotton delivered C.I.F. Northern Europe; and
the Northern Europe price.

subsection.heading: Availability of Loan Deficiency Payments.—
subsection.chapeau: Except as provided in subsection (d), the Secretary may make loan deficiency payments available to—

paragraph.content: producers who, although eligible to obtain a marketing assistance loan under section 131 with respect to a loan commodity, agree to forgo obtaining the loan for the commodity in return for payments under this section; and
effective only for the 2000 and 2001 crop years, producers that, although not eligible to obtain such a marketing assistance loan under section 131, produce a contract commodity.

subsection.heading: Computation.—
subsection.chapeau: A loan deficiency payment under this section shall be computed by multiplying—

paragraph.content: the loan payment rate determined under subsection (c) for the loan commodity; by
the quantity of the loan commodity produced by the eligible producers, excluding any quantity for which the producers obtain a loan under section 131.

subsection.heading: Loan Payment Rate.—
subsection.chapeau: For purposes of this section, the loan payment rate shall be the amount by which—

paragraph.content: the loan rate established under section 132 for the loan commodity; exceeds
the rate at which a loan for the commodity may be repaid under section 134.

subsection.heading: Exception for Extra Long Staple Cotton.—
subsection.content: This section shall not apply with respect to extra long staple cotton.

subsection.heading: Transition.—
subsection.content: A payment to a producer eligible for a payment under subsection (a)(2) that harvested a commodity on or before the date that is 30 days after the promulgation of the regulations implementing subsection (a)(2) shall be determined as the date the producer lost beneficial interest in the commodity, as determined by the Secretary.

subsection.heading: Beneficial Interest.—
subsection.content: Subject to subsection (e), a producer shall be eligible for a payment under this section only if the producer has a beneficial interest in the commodity, as determined by the Secretary.

subsection.heading: Effective Date for Payment Rate Determination.—
subsection.chapeau: For the 2001 crop year, the Secretary shall determine the amount of the loan deficiency payment to be made under this section to the producers on a farm with respect to a quantity of a loan commodity using the payment rate in effect under subsection (c) as of the earlier of the following:

paragraph.content: The date on which the producers marketed or otherwise lost beneficial interest in the crop of the loan commodity, as determined by the Secretary.
The date the producers requested the payment.

section.heading: SPECIAL MARKETING LOAN PROVISIONS FOR UPLAND COTTON.4

footnote.p: Sec. 1207 of the Farm Security and Rural Investment Act of 2002 (7 U.S.C. 7937; P.L. 107–171, 116 Stat. 161, May 13, 2002) contains provisions that are substantively similar to this section, other than later expiration dates in, and subsecs. (a)(4) and (b)(1)(E) of, sec. 1207 of that Act. Since sec. 1207 of that Act was enacted later in time than this sec., it is the probable intent of Congress that sec. 1207 of that Act supersedes this sec.

paragraph.heading: Issuance.—
paragraph.chapeau: During the period ending July 31, 2003, the Secretary shall issue marketing certificates or cash payments, at the option of the recipient, to domestic users and exporters for documented purchases by domestic users and sales for export by exporters made in the week following a consecutive 4-week period in which—

subparagraph.content: the Friday through Thursday average price quotation for the lowest-priced United States growth, as quoted for Middling (M) 13⁄32-inch cotton, delivered C.I.F. Northern Europe exceeds the Northern Europe price by more than 1.25 cents per pound; and
the prevailing world market price for upland cotton (adjusted to United States quality and location) does not exceed 134 percent of the loan rate for upland cotton established under section 132.

paragraph.heading: Value of certificates or payments.—
paragraph.content: The value of the marketing certificates or cash payments shall be based on the amount of the difference (reduced by 1.25 cents per pound) in the prices during the 4th week of the consecutive 4-week period multiplied by the quantity of upland cotton included in the documented sales.

subparagraph.heading: Redemption, marketing, or exchange.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall establish procedures for redeeming marketing certificates for cash or marketing or exchange of the certificates for agricultural commodities owned by the Commodity Credit Corporation or pledged to the Commodity Credit Corporation as collateral for a loan in such manner, and at such price levels, as the Secretary determines will best effectuate the purposes of cotton user marketing certificates, including enhancing the competitiveness and marketability of United States cotton. Any price restrictions that would otherwise apply to the disposition of agricultural commodities by the Commodity Credit Corporation shall not apply to the redemption of certificates under this subsection.

subparagraph.heading: Designation of commodities and products.—
subparagraph.content: To the extent practicable, the Secretary shall permit owners of certificates to designate the commodities and products, including storage sites, the owners would prefer to receive in exchange for certificates.

subparagraph.heading: Transfers.—
subparagraph.content: Marketing certificates issued to domestic users and exporters of upland cotton may be transferred to other persons in accordance with regulations issued by the Secretary.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The President shall carry out an import quota program during the period ending July 31, 2003, as provided in this subsection.

subparagraph.heading: Program requirements.—
subparagraph.content: Except as provided in subparagraph (C), whenever the Secretary determines and announces that for any consecutive 4-week period, the Friday through Thursday average price quotation for the lowest-priced United States growth, as quoted for Middling (M) 13⁄32-inch cotton, delivered C.I.F. Northern Europe, adjusted for the value of any certificate issued under subsection (a), exceeds the Northern Europe price by more than 1.25 cents per pound, there shall immediately be in effect a special import quota.

subparagraph.heading: Tight domestic supply.—
subparagraph.content: During any month for which the Secretary estimates the season-ending United States upland cotton stocks-to-use ratio, as determined under subparagraph (D), to be below 16 percent, the Secretary, in making the determination under subparagraph (B), shall not adjust the Friday through Thursday average price quotation for the lowest-priced United States growth, as quoted for Middling (M) 13⁄32-inch cotton, delivered C.I.F. Northern Europe, for the value of any certificates issued under subsection (a).

subparagraph.heading: Season-ending united states stocks-to-use ratio.—
subparagraph.content: For the purposes of making estimates under subparagraph (C), the Secretary shall, on a monthly basis, estimate and report the season-ending United States upland cotton stocks-to-use ratio, excluding projected raw cotton imports but including the quantity of raw cotton that has been imported into the United States during the marketing year.

paragraph.heading: Quantity.—
paragraph.content: The quota shall be equal to 1 week's consumption of upland cotton by domestic mills at the seasonally adjusted average rate of the most recent 3 months for which data are available.

paragraph.heading: Application.—
paragraph.content: The quota shall apply to upland cotton purchased not later than 90 days after the date of the Secretary's announcement under paragraph (1) and entered into the United States not later than 180 days after the date.

paragraph.heading: Overlap.—
paragraph.content: A special quota period may be established that overlaps any existing quota period if required by paragraph (1), except that a special quota period may not be established under this subsection if a quota period has been established under subsection (c).

paragraph.heading: Preferential tariff treatment.—
paragraph.chapeau: The quantity under a special import quota shall be considered to be an in-quota quantity for purposes of—

subparagraph.content: section 213(d) of the Caribbean Basin Economic Recovery Act (19 U.S.C. 2703(d));
section 204 of the Andean Trade Preference Act (19 U.S.C. 3203);
section 503(d) of the Trade Act of 1974 (19 U.S.C. 2463(d)); and
General Note 3(a)(iv) to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule.

paragraph.heading: Definition.—
paragraph.content: In this subsection, the term “special import quota” means a quantity of imports that is not subject to the over-quota tariff rate of a tariff-rate quota.

paragraph.heading: Limitation.—
paragraph.content: The quantity of cotton entered into the United States during any marketing year under the special import quota established under this subsection may not exceed the equivalent of 5 week's consumption of upland cotton by domestic mills at the seasonally adjusted average rate of the 3 months immediately preceding the first special import quota established in any marketing year.

subsection.heading: Limited Global Import Quota for Upland Cotton.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The President shall carry out an import quota program that provides that whenever the Secretary determines and announces that the average price of the base quality of upland cotton, as determined by the Secretary, in the designated spot markets for a month exceeded 130 percent of the average price of such quality of cotton in the markets for the preceding 36 months, notwithstanding any other provision of law, there shall immediately be in effect a limited global import quota subject to the following conditions:

subparagraph.heading: Quantity.—
subparagraph.content: The quantity of the quota shall be equal to 21 days of domestic mill consumption of upland cotton at the seasonally adjusted average rate of the most recent 3 months for which data are available.

subparagraph.heading: Quantity if prior quota.—
subparagraph.content: If a quota has been established under this subsection during the preceding 12 months, the quantity of the quota next established under this subsection shall be the smaller of 21 days of domestic mill consumption calculated under subparagraph (A) or the quantity required to increase the supply to 130 percent of the demand.

subparagraph.heading: Preferential tariff treatment.—
subparagraph.chapeau: The quantity under a limited global import quota shall be considered to be an in-quota quantity for purposes of—

clause.content: section 213(d) of the Caribbean Basin Economic Recovery Act (19 U.S.C. 2703(d));
section 204 of the Andean Trade Preference Act (19 U.S.C. 3203);
section 503(d) of the Trade Act of 1974 (19 U.S.C. 2463(d)); and
General Note 3(a)(iv) to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule.

subparagraph.heading: Definitions.—
subparagraph.chapeau: In this subsection:

clause.heading: Supply.—
clause.chapeau: The term “supply” means, using the latest official data of the Bureau of the Census, the Department of Agriculture, and the Department of the Treasury—

subclause.content: the carry-over of upland cotton at the beginning of the marketing year (adjusted to 480-pound bales) in which the quota is established;
production of the current crop; and
imports to the latest date available during the marketing year.
the average seasonally adjusted annual rate of domestic mill consumption during the most recent 3 months for which data are available; and

item.content: average exports of upland cotton during the preceding 6 marketing years; or
cumulative exports of upland cotton plus outstanding export sales for the marketing year in which the quota is established.

clause.heading: Limited global import quota.—
clause.content: The term “limited global import quota” means a quantity of imports that is not subject to the over-quota tariff rate of a tariff-rate quota.

subparagraph.heading: Quota entry period.—
subparagraph.content: When a quota is established under this subsection, cotton may be entered under the quota during the 90-day period beginning on the date the quota is established by the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: No overlap.—
paragraph.content: Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a quota period may not be established that overlaps an existing quota period or a special quota period established under subsection (b).

Since sec. 1208 of that Act was enacted later in time than this sec., it is the probable intent of Congress that sec. 1208 of that Act supersedes this sec.

subsection.heading: Competitiveness Program.—
subsection.content: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, during the period beginning on October 1, 1999, and ending on July 31, 2003, the Secretary shall carry out a program to maintain and expand the domestic use of extra long staple cotton produced in the United States, to increase exports of extra long staple cotton produced in the United States, and to ensure that extra long staple cotton produced in the United States remains competitive in world markets.

subsection.heading: Payments Under Program; Trigger.—
subsection.chapeau: Under the program, the Secretary shall make payments available under this section whenever—

paragraph.content: for a consecutive 4-week period, the world market price for the lowest priced competing growth of extra long staple cotton (adjusted to United States quality and location and for other factors affecting the competitiveness of such cotton), as determined by the Secretary, is below the prevailing United States price for a competing growth of extra long staple cotton; and

the lowest priced competing growth of extra long staple cotton (adjusted to United States quality and location and for other factors affecting the competitiveness of such cotton), as determined by the Secretary, is less than 134 percent of the loan rate for extra long staple cotton.

subsection.heading: Eligible Recipients.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall make payments available under this section to domestic users of extra long staple cotton produced in the United States and exporters of extra long staple cotton produced in the United States who enter into an agreement with the Commodity Credit Corporation to participate in the program under this section.

subsection.heading: Payment Amount.—
subsection.content: Payments under this section shall be based on the amount of the difference in the prices referred to in subsection (b)(1) during the fourth week of the consecutive 4-week period multiplied by the amount of documented purchases by domestic users and sales for export by exporters made in the week following such a consecutive 4-week period.

subsection.heading: Form of Payment.—
subsection.content: Payments under this section shall be made through the issuance of cash or marketing certificates, at the option of eligible recipients of the payments.

section.heading: AVAILABILITY OF RECOURSE LOANS FOR HIGH MOISTURE FEED GRAINS AND SEED COTTON AND OTHER FIBERS.

paragraph.heading: Recourse loans available.—
paragraph.chapeau: For each of the 1996 through 2002 crops of corn and grain sorghum, the Secretary shall make available recourse loans, as determined by the Secretary, to producers on a farm containing eligible cropland covered by a production flexibility contract who—

subparagraph.content: normally harvest all or a portion of their crop of corn or grain sorghum in a high moisture state;

subparagraph.chapeau: present—

clause.content: certified scale tickets from an inspected, certified commercial scale, including a licensed warehouse, feedlot, feed mill, distillery, or other similar entity approved by the Secretary, pursuant to regulations issued by the Secretary; or

field or other physical measurements of the standing or stored crop in regions of the United States, as determined by the Secretary, that do not have certified commercial scales from which certified scale tickets may be obtained within reasonable proximity of harvest operation;

subparagraph.content: certify that they were the owners of the feed grain at the time of delivery to, and that the quantity to be placed under loan under this subsection was in fact harvested on the farm and delivered to, a feedlot, feed mill, or commercial or on-farm high-moisture storage facility, or to a facility maintained by the users of corn and grain sorghum in a high moisture state; and
comply with deadlines established by the Secretary for harvesting the corn or grain sorghum and submit applications for loans under this subsection within deadlines established by the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Eligibility of acquired feed grains.—
paragraph.chapeau: A loan under this subsection shall be made on a quantity of corn or grain sorghum of the same crop acquired by the producer equivalent to a quantity determined by multiplying—

subparagraph.content: the acreage of the corn or grain sorghum in a high moisture state harvested on the producer's farm; by
the lower of the farm program payment yield or the actual yield on a field, as determined by the Secretary, that is similar to the field from which the corn or grain sorghum was obtained.

paragraph.heading: High moisture state defined.—
paragraph.content: In this subsection, the term “high moisture state” means corn or grain sorghum having a moisture content in excess of Commodity Credit Corporation standards for marketing assistance loans made by the Secretary under section 131.

subsection.heading: Recourse Loans Available for Seed Cotton.—

paragraph.heading: Upland cotton.—
paragraph.content: For each of the 1996 through 2002 crops of upland cotton, the Secretary shall make available recourse seed cotton loans, as determined by the Secretary, to producers on a farm containing eligible cropland covered by a production flexibility contract.

paragraph.heading: Extra long staple cotton.—
paragraph.content: For each of the 1996 through 2002 crops of extra long staple cotton, the Secretary shall make available recourse seed cotton loans, as determined by the Secretary, on any production.

paragraph.heading: Recourse loans available.—
paragraph.content: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, during fiscal year 1999, the Secretary shall make available recourse loans, as determined by the Secretary, to producers of mohair produced during or before that fiscal year.

paragraph.heading: Loan rate.—
paragraph.content: The loan rate for a loan under paragraph (1) shall be equal to $2.00 per pound.

paragraph.heading: Term of loan.—
paragraph.content: A loan under paragraph (1) shall have a term of 1 year beginning on the first day of the first month after the month in which the loan is made.

paragraph.heading: Waiver of interest.—
paragraph.content: Notwithstanding subsection (d), the Secretary shall not charge interest on a loan made under paragraph (1).

subsection.heading: Repayment Rates.—
subsection.content: Repayment of a recourse loan made under this section shall be at the loan rate established for the commodity by the Secretary, plus interest (as determined by the Secretary).

subsection.heading: Support Activities.—
subsection.content: The Secretary of Agriculture shall support the price of milk produced in the 48 contiguous States through the purchase of cheese, butter, and nonfat dry milk produced from the milk.

subsection.heading: Rate.—
subsection.chapeau: The price of milk shall be supported at the following rates per hundredweight for milk containing 3.67 percent butterfat:

paragraph.content: During calendar year 1996, $10.35.
During calendar year 1997, $10.20.
During calendar year 1998, $10.05.
During each of calendar years 1999 through 2001, $9.90.
During the period beginning on January 1, 2002, and ending on May 31, 2002, $9.90.

subsection.heading: Purchase Prices.—
subsection.content: The support purchase prices under this section for each of the products of milk (butter, cheese, and nonfat dry milk) announced by the Secretary shall be the same for all of that product sold by persons offering to sell the product to the Secretary. The purchase prices shall be sufficient to enable plants of average efficiency to pay producers, on average, a price that is not less than the rate of price support for milk in effect under subsection (b).

subsection.heading: Special Rule for Butter and Nonfat Dry Milk Purchase Prices.—

paragraph.heading: Allocation of purchase prices.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may allocate the rate of price support between the purchase prices for nonfat dry milk and butter in a manner that will result in the lowest level of expenditures by the Commodity Credit Corporation or achieve such other objectives as the Secretary considers appropriate. Not later than 10 days after making or changing an allocation, the Secretary shall notify the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate of the allocation. Section 553 of title 5, United States Code, shall not apply with respect to the implementation of this section.

paragraph.heading: Timing of purchase price adjustments.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary may make any such adjustments in the purchase prices for nonfat dry milk and butter the Secretary considers to be necessary not more than twice in each calendar year.

paragraph.heading: Refund required.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall provide for a refund of the entire reduction required under section 204(h)(2) of the Agricultural Act of 1949 (7 U.S.C. 1446e(h)(2)), as in effect on the day before the amendment made by subsection (g), in the price of milk received by a producer during calendar year 1995 or 1996, if the producer provides evidence that the producer did not increase marketings in calendar year 1995 or 1996 when compared to calendar year 1994 or 1995, respectively.

paragraph.heading: Exception.—
paragraph.content: This subsection shall not apply with respect to a producer for a particular calendar year if the producer has already received a refund under section 204(h) of the Agricultural Act of 1949 for the same fiscal year before the effective date of this section.

paragraph.heading: Treatment of refund.—
paragraph.content: A refund under this subsection shall not be considered as any type of price support or payment for purposes of sections 1211 and 1221 of the Food Security Act of 1985 (16 U.S.C. 3811 and 3821).

subsection.heading: Commodity Credit Corporation.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall carry out the program authorized by this section through the Commodity Credit Corporation.

subsection.heading: Period of Effectiveness.—
subsection.content: This section (other than subsection (g)) shall be effective only during the period beginning on the first day of the first month beginning after the date of enactment of this title and ending on May 31, 2002. section.heading: CONSOLIDATION AND REFORM OF FEDERAL MILK MARKETING ORDERS.

paragraph.heading: Required consolidation.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall amend Federal milk marketing orders issued under section 8c of the Agricultural Adjustment Act (7 U.S.C. 608c), reenacted with amendments by the Agricultural Marketing Agreement Act of 1937, to limit the number of Federal milk marketing orders to not less than 10 and not more than 14 orders.

paragraph.heading: Inclusion of california as separate order.—
paragraph.content: Upon the petition and approval of California dairy producers in the manner provided in section 8c of the Agricultural Adjustment Act (7 U.S.C. 608c), reenacted with amendments by the Agricultural Marketing Agreement Act of 1937, the Secretary shall designate the State of California as a separate Federal milk marketing order. The order covering California shall have the right to reblend and distribute order receipts to recognize quota value. Subsection (b) does not apply to the authority of the Secretary under this subsection.

paragraph.heading: Related issues addressed in consolidation.—
paragraph.chapeau: Among the issues the Secretary is authorized to implement as part of the consolidation of Federal milk marketing orders are the following:

subparagraph.content: The use of utilization rates and multiple basing points for the pricing of fluid milk.
The use of uniform multiple component pricing when developing 1 or more basic formula prices for manufacturing milk.

paragraph.heading: Effect of existing law.—
paragraph.content: In implementing the consolidation of Federal milk marketing orders and related reforms under this subsection, the Secretary may not consider, or base any decision on, the table contained in section 8c(5)(A) of the Agricultural Adjustment Act (7 U.S.C. 608c(5)(A)), reenacted with amendments by the Agricultural Marketing Agreement Act of 1937, as added by section 131 of the Food Security Act of 1985.

paragraph.heading: Use of informal rulemaking.—
paragraph.content: To implement the consolidation of Federal milk marketing orders and related reforms under subsection (a), the Secretary shall use the notice and comment procedures provided in section 553 of title 5, United States Code.

subparagraph.heading: Proposed amendments.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall announce the proposed amendments to be made under subsection (a) not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this title.

subparagraph.heading: Final amendments.—
subparagraph.content: The Secretary shall implement the amendments not later than 3 years after the date of enactment of this title.

paragraph.heading: Effect of court order.—
paragraph.content: The actions authorized by this subsection are intended to ensure the timely publication and implementation of new and amended Federal milk marketing orders. In the event that the Secretary is enjoined or otherwise restrained by a court order from publishing or implementing the consolidation and related reforms under subsection (a), the length of time for which that injunction or other restraining order is effective shall be added to the time limitations specified in paragraph (2) thereby extending those time limitations by a period of time equal to the period of time for which the injunction or other restraining order is effective.

subsection.heading: Failure To Timely Consolidate Orders.—
subsection.content: If the Secretary fails to implement the consolidation required under subsection (a)(1) within the time period required under subsection (b)(2)(B) (plus any additional period provided under subsection (b)(3)), the Secretary may not assess or collect assessments from milk producers or handlers under such section 8c for marketing order administration and services provided under such section after the end of that period until the consolidation is completed. The Secretary may not reduce the level of services provided under the section on account of the prohibition against assessments, but shall rather cover the cost of marketing order administration and services through funds available for the Agricultural Marketing Service of the Department.

paragraph.heading: Report required.—
paragraph.chapeau: Not later than April 1, 1997, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report—

subparagraph.content: reviewing the Federal milk marketing order system established pursuant to section 8c of the Agricultural Adjustment Act (7 U.S.C. 608c), reenacted with amendments by the Agricultural Marketing Agreement Act of 1937, in light of the reforms required by subsection (a);
describing the efforts underway and the progress made in implementing the reforms required by subsection (a); and
containing such recommendations as the Secretary considers appropriate for further improvements and reforms to the Federal milk marketing order system.

paragraph.heading: Effect of other laws.—
paragraph.content: Any limitation imposed by Act of Congress on the conduct or completion of reports to Congress shall not apply to the report required under this section, unless the limitation specifically refers to this section.

section.heading: EFFECT ON FLUID MILK STANDARDS IN STATE OF CALIFORNIA.

subsection.chapeau: Nothing in this Act or any other provision of law shall be construed to preempt, prohibit, or otherwise limit the authority of the State of California, directly or indirectly, to establish or continue to effect any law, regulation, or requirement regarding—

paragraph.content: the percentage of milk solids or solids not fat in fluid milk products sold at retail or marketed in the State of California; or
the labeling of such fluid milk products with regard to milk solids or solids not fat.

subsection.heading: Maximum Allowances Established.—
subsection.chapeau: No State shall provide for a manufacturing allowance for the processing of milk in excess of—

paragraph.content: $1.65 per hundredweight of milk for milk manufactured into butter and nonfat dry milk; and
$1.80 per hundredweight of milk for milk manufactured into cheese.

subsection.heading: Manufacturing Allowance Defined.—
subsection.chapeau: In this section, the term “manufacturing allowance” means—

paragraph.content: the amount by which the product price value of butter and nonfat dry milk manufactured from a hundred pounds of milk containing 3.5 pounds of butterfat and 8.7 pounds of milk solids not fat resulting from a State's yield and product price formulas exceeds the class price for the milk used to produce those products; or

the amount by which the product price value of cheese manufactured from a hundred pounds of milk containing 3.5 pounds of butterfat and 8.7 pounds of milk solids not fat resulting from a State's yield and product price formulas exceeds the class price for the milk used to produce cheese.

subsection.heading: Effect of Violation.—
subsection.content: If the Secretary determines following a hearing that a State has in effect a manufacturing allowance that exceeds the manufacturing allowance authorized in subsection (a), the Secretary shall suspend purchases of cheddar cheese, butter, and nonfat dry milk produced in that State until such time as the State complies with such subsection.

subsection.heading: Effective Date; Implementation.—
subsection.content: This section (other than subsection (e)) shall be effective during the period beginning on the first day of the first month beginning after the date of enactment of this title and ending on December 31, 1999. During that period, the Secretary may exercise the authority provided to the Secretary under this section without regard to the issuance of regulations intended to carry out this section.

subsection.chapeau: Congress hereby consents to the Northeast Interstate Dairy Compact entered into among the States of Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island and Vermont as specified in section 1(b) Senate Joint Resolution 28 of the 104th Congress, as placed on the calendar of the Senate, subject to the following conditions:

paragraph.heading: Finding of compelling public interest.—
paragraph.content: Based upon a finding by the Secretary of a compelling public interest in the Compact region, the Secretary may grant the States that have ratified the Northeast Interstate Dairy Compact, as of the date of enactment of this title, the authority to implement the Northeast Interstate Dairy Compact.

paragraph.heading: Limitation on manufacturing price.—
paragraph.content: The Northeast Interstate Dairy Compact Commission shall not regulate Class II, Class III, or Class III-A milk used for manufacturing purposes or any other milk, other than Class I (fluid) milk, as defined by a Federal milk marketing order issued under section 8c of the Agricultural Adjustment Act (7 U.S.C. 608c) reenacted with amendments by the Agricultural Marketing Agreement Act of 1937.

paragraph.heading: Duration.—
paragraph.content: Consent for the Northeast Interstate Dairy Compact shall terminate on September 30, 2001.

paragraph.heading: Additional states.—
paragraph.content: Delaware, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Maryland, and Virginia are the only additional States that may join the Northeast Interstate Dairy Compact, individually or otherwise, if upon entry the State is contiguous to a participating State and if Congress consents to the entry of the State into the Compact after the date of enactment of this title.

paragraph.heading: Compensation of commodity credit corporation.—
paragraph.content: Before the end of each fiscal year that a Compact price regulation is in effect, the Northeast Interstate Dairy Compact Commission shall compensate the Commodity Credit Corporation for the cost of any purchases of milk and milk products by the Corporation that result from the projected rate of increase in milk production for the fiscal year within the Compact region in excess of the projected national average rate of the increase in milk production, as determined by the Secretary.

paragraph.heading: Milk marketing order administrator.—
paragraph.content: At the request of the Northeast Interstate Dairy Compact Commission, the Administrator of the applicable Federal milk marketing order issued under section 8(c)5 of the Agricultural Adjustment Act (7 U.S.C. 608c), reenacted with amendments by the Agricultural Marketing Agreement Act of 1937, shall provide technical assistance to the Compact Commission and be compensated for that assistance.

paragraph.heading: Further conditions.—
paragraph.content: The Northeast Interstate Dairy Compact Commission shall not prohibit or in any way limit the marketing in the Compact region of any milk or milk product produced in any other production area in the United States. The Compact Commission shall respect and abide by the ongoing procedures between Federal milk marketing orders with respect to the sharing of proceeds from sales within the Compact region of bulk milk, packaged milk, or producer milk originating from outside of the Compact region. The Compact Commission shall not use compensatory payments under section 10(6) of the Compact as a barrier to the entry of milk into the Compact region or for any other purpose. Establishment of a Compact over-order price, in itself, shall not be considered a compensatory payment or a limitation or prohibition on the marketing of milk.

section.heading: AUTHORITY TO ASSIST IN ESTABLISHMENT AND MAINTENANCE OF ONE OR MORE EXPORT TRADING COMPANIES.
section.content: The Secretary of Agriculture shall, consistent with the obligations of the United States as a member of the World Trade Organization, provide such advice and assistance to the United States dairy industry as may be necessary to enable that industry to establish and maintain one or more export trading companies under the Export Trading Company Act of 1982 (15 U.S.C. 4001 et seq.) for the purpose of facilitating the international market development for and exportation of dairy products produced in the United States.

section.heading: STANDBY AUTHORITY TO INDICATE ENTITY BEST SUITED TO PROVIDE INTERNATIONAL MARKET DEVELOPMENT AND EXPORT SERVICES.

subsection.heading: Indication of Entity Best Suited To Assist International Market Development for and Export of United States Dairy Products.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary of Agriculture shall indicate which entity or entities autonomous of the Government of the United States, which seeks such a designation, is best suited to facilitate the international market development for and exportation of United States dairy products, if the Secretary determines that—

paragraph.content: the United States dairy industry has not established an export trading company under the Export Trading Company Act of 1982 (15 U.S.C. 4001 et seq.) for the purpose of facilitating the international market development for an exportation of dairy products produced in the United States on or before June 30, 1997; or

the quantity of exports of United States dairy products during the 12-month period preceding July 1, 1998 does not exceed the quantity of exports of United States dairy products during the 12-month period preceding July 1, 1997 by 1.5 billion pounds (milk equivalent, total solids basis).

subsection.heading: Funding of Export Activities.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall assist the entity or entities identified under subsection (a) in identifying sources of funding for the activities specified in subsection (a) from within the dairy industry and elsewhere.

subsection.heading: Application of Section.—
subsection.content: This section shall apply only during the period beginning on July 1, 1997 and ending on September 30, 2000.

section.heading: STUDY AND REPORT REGARDING POTENTIAL IMPACT OF URUGUAY ROUND ON PRICES, INCOME, AND GOVERNMENT PURCHASES.

subsection.heading: Study.—
subsection.content: The Secretary of Agriculture shall conduct a study, on a variety by variety of cheese basis, to determine the potential impact on milk prices in the United States, dairy producer income, and Federal dairy program costs, of the allocation of additional cheese granted access to the United States as a result of the obligations of the United States as a member of the World Trade Organization.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.content: Not later than June 30, 1997, the Secretary shall report to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate and the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives the results of the study conducted under this section.

subsection.heading: Rule of Construction.—
subsection.content: Any limitation imposed by Act of Congress on the conduct or completion of studies or reports to Congress shall not apply to the study and report required under this section, unless the limitation specifically refers to this section.

section.heading: PROMOTION OF UNITED STATES DAIRY PRODUCTS IN INTERNATIONAL MARKETS THROUGH DAIRY PROMOTION PROGRAM.11
